description: Create the CloudFormation infrastructure under infra/ for the programming-course app in us-east-1. This is the foundation all other features reference; it defines the exact resource names, ports, path patterns, and Cognito settings the backend and frontend must match. Split into logical templates (network+security, storage+CDN, auth, compute) plus an infra/README.md documenting deploy order, parameters, and outputs. All infrastructure must be repeatable and idempotent.
steps: Create infra/README.md describing the stacks, required deploy-time Parameters (GoogleClientId, GoogleClientSecret, BackendImageTag/ECR image URI, optional ACM cert + domain), deploy order, and how outputs wire together. Explicitly list values the user must supply at deploy time.

infra/network.yaml: VPC with 2 public + 2 private subnets across 2 AZs (us-east-1a/b), IGW, NAT gateway(s) for private subnet egress, route tables. Internet-facing ALB in public subnets with a security group allowing 80 (and 443 if cert provided). ALB HTTP listener with a target group of type 'ip' (Fargate awsvpc) whose health check path is '/health' on the container port 8000, matcher 200. Output: ALB DNS name, ALB listener ARN, target group ARN, VPC id, subnet ids, ALB security group id.

infra/security.yaml (or a WAF section): AWS::WAFv2::WebACL scope REGIONAL for the ALB with managed rule groups AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet, AWSManagedRulesKnownBadInputsRuleSet, and a rate-based rule (e.g., 2000 req/5min per IP). Associate the REGIONAL WebACL with the ALB via AWS::WAFv2::WebACLAssociation. Note: CloudFront-scoped WAF (scope CLOUDFRONT, us-east-1) is optional; if included it must be a separate WebACL. Keep the ALB REGIONAL WebACL as the required one.

infra/storage.yaml: (a) Content bucket AWS::S3::BucketName 'course-content-<postfix>' where postfix is derived from the stack to stay repeatable, e.g. !Select [2, !Split ['/', !Ref AWS::StackId]] giving the stack's unique GUID segment, so name = !Sub 'course-content-${UniqueSuffix}'. Block public access on this bucket (it is accessed by the backend via IAM, not publicly). (b) SPA hosting bucket for the static Next.js export, private, accessed only by CloudFront via Origin Access Control (OAC). (c) CloudFront distribution: default cache behavior -> S3 SPA origin (OAC) serving index.html with SPA custom error responses (403/404 -> /index.html 200); an ordered cache behavior for path pattern '/api/*' -> ALB origin (custom origin, HTTP or HTTPS) with CachePolicyId = CachingDisabled (4135ea2d-6df8-44a3-9df3-4b5a84be39ad) and an OriginRequestPolicy that forwards all viewer headers incl. Authorization + query strings (AllViewer = 216adef6-5c7f-47e4-b989-5492eeaf6572). Outputs: content bucket name, SPA bucket name, CloudFront domain name, CloudFront distribution id.

infra/auth.yaml: AWS::Cognito::UserPool (no native sign-up needed; email as username attribute). AWS::Cognito::UserPoolIdentityProvider of ProviderType 'Google' using GoogleClientId/GoogleClientSecret parameters, authorize scopes 'openid email profile', attribute mapping email->email. AWS::Cognito::UserPoolClient with SupportedIdentityProviders ['Google'] ONLY (no COGNITO), AllowedOAuthFlows ['code'], AllowedOAuthScopes ['openid','email','profile'], AllowedOAuthFlowsUserPoolClient true, GenerateSecret false (public SPA client uses PKCE), CallbackURLs and LogoutURLs referencing the CloudFront domain (parameterize an app URL or build from CloudFront output). AWS::Cognito::UserPoolDomain with a domain prefix parameter and ManagedLoginVersion: 2 (new Managed Login). AWS::Cognito::ManagedLoginBranding with UseCognitoProvidedValues: true for the client. Outputs: user pool id, user pool client id, Cognito domain (full URL), the token issuer URL, and JWKS URL.

infra/compute.yaml: AWS::ECR::Repository 'course-backend'. ECS cluster with FARGATE and FARGATE_SPOT capacity providers. Task definition (awsvpc, 256 cpu/512 mem, container port 8000) referencing the ECR image (parameter for image tag/URI), with env vars COGNITO_USER_POOL_ID, COGNITO_REGION=us-east-1, COGNITO_CLIENT_ID, COGNITO_ISSUER, AWS_REGION, CONTENT_BUCKET, PORT=8000. Task role: IAM policy granting s3:GetObject/PutObject/ListBucket on the content bucket ARN and objects. Execution role: pull from ECR + CloudWatch logs. ECS service using capacity provider strategy FARGATE_SPOT (weight 1, base 0), desired count 1, in private subnets, registered to the ALB target group, with a service security group allowing inbound 8000 only from the ALB security group. CloudWatch log group. Outputs: ECR repo URI, service name, cluster name.

Ensure every cross-file reference is consistent: container port 8000 everywhere, health check path /health, API path pattern /api/*, content bucket name 'course-content-<suffix>', and Cognito outputs named so backend env vars and frontend config can consume them. Use consistent Export names if using ImportValue across stacks; document them in infra/README.md.
acceptance_criteria: Every YAML file in infra/ parses without error using a CloudFormation-aware loader (cfn-lint if available, otherwise a YAML load that tolerates CFN intrinsic short forms).
The content S3 bucket resource yields a name of the form 'course-content-<dynamic-suffix>' derived from AWS::StackId (no hardcoded random string).
The Cognito UserPoolClient lists Google as the only supported identity provider, uses OAuth flow 'code', GenerateSecret false, and the domain uses ManagedLoginVersion 2.

The CloudFront distribution has a default behavior to the S3 SPA origin and an ordered '/api/*' behavior to the ALB origin with the CachingDisabled cache policy and a header-forwarding origin request policy.
The WAFv2 WebACL (REGIONAL) includes common rule set, known bad inputs, and a rate-based rule, and is associated with the ALB.
The ECS service uses the FARGATE_SPOT capacity provider, the task role grants access to the content bucket, and the ALB target group health check targets /health on port 8000.
infra/README.md lists deploy order and every deploy-time parameter (GoogleClientId, GoogleClientSecret, image tag/URI, domain prefix, optional ACM cert/domain).
verification: Run: pip install cfn-lint && cfn-lint infra/*.yaml (report results). If cfn-lint cannot install, run a python script using cfnlint or a yaml loader with CFN tag support (e.g. cfn_flip / a custom SafeLoader registering !Ref,!Sub,!GetAtt,!Select,!Split,!Join,!Sub) and confirm all templates load.
Grep-independent consistency check: confirm port 8000, '/health', and '/api/*' appear consistently across network.yaml, compute.yaml, and storage.yaml.
findings: Implemented 5 CloudFormation templates under infra/ (network.yaml, security.yaml, storage.yaml, auth.yaml, compute.yaml) plus infra/README.md. All validated clean with cfn-lint 1.46.0 (installed to /usr/local/bin/cfn-lint under python3.9; invoke via that path, not `python3 -m cfnlint`). Consistency verified: container port 8000, health path /health, and /api/* appear consistently across network/compute/storage. Content bucket name is course-content-${!Select[2,!Split['/',AWS::StackId]]} (stack GUID segment, repeatable, no hardcoded random). Cognito client lists Google as the ONLY SupportedIdentityProvider, AllowedOAuthFlows=[code], GenerateSecret=false; UserPoolDomain ManagedLoginVersion=2 with ManagedLoginBranding UseCognitoProvidedValues=true. CloudFront default behavior -> SPA S3 origin (OAC, CachingOptimized) with 403/404->/index.html SPA fallbacks, and ordered /api/* -> ALB origin using CachingDisabled cache policy 4135ea2d-6df8-44a3-9df3-4b5a84be39ad + AllViewer origin request policy 216adef6-5c7f-47e4-b989-5492eeaf6572. WAFv2 REGIONAL WebACL (CommonRuleSet + KnownBadInputs + rate-based 2000/5min) associated with the ALB. ECS service uses FARGATE_SPOT (weight 1, base 0), task role grants s3 List/Get/Put on the content bucket, ALB IP target group health check /health:8000 matcher 200. Cross-stack wiring uses Fn::ImportValue with ${AWS::StackName}-<Output> export names; downstream stacks take upstream stack names as parameters. Deploy-time params (GoogleClientId/Secret, CognitoDomainPrefix, AppUrl, BackendImageUri/Tag, optional ACM CertificateArn + DomainName) documented in infra/README.md. Note for later features: content bucket ARN export is ${StorageStackName}-ContentBucketArn, bucket name export ${StorageStackName}-ContentBucketName; auth exports UserPoolId/UserPoolClientId/CognitoDomainUrl/IssuerUrl/JwksUrl. AppUrl output comes from the storage stack, so deploy storage before auth on a first deploy to obtain the CloudFront domain for OAuth callbacks.
